slides.title: He said he was Jesus's brother. Millions died in his war.
Failed four times
slides.body: Hong Xiuquan, from a Hakka farming family near Guangzhou, failed the qualifying exam for China's civil service four times. In 1837 he fell ill and had visions.

slides.title: A sword from heaven
slides.body: In the later Taiping account, he was carried to heaven, where an old man with a golden beard gave him a sword and a seal and ordered him to slay demons.

slides.title: God's second son
slides.body: In 1843 he properly read some Christian tracts and decided: the old man was God, his elder brother was Jesus, and Hong was God's second son.

slides.title: The Heavenly Kingdom
slides.body: In 1851 he proclaimed the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace. In 1853 his armies took Nanjing, renamed it the Heavenly Capital and held it for 11 years.

slides.title: 20 to 30 million dead
slides.body: That's what most historians estimate, chiefly from famine and disease alongside battle and massacre. Some estimates run much higher.

caption: He failed an exam four times, fell ill, had visions, and decided he was God's second son. What followed was one of history's deadliest wars. Had you heard of it?
